title: a hollow that does not finish stops prove.sh loudly
intention: prove.sh's hollow step runs the hollow to its end under the hollow verb's own per-run bound, and a hollow that does not finish stops prove.sh with exit 6 and a line naming its exit status, instead of exiting 0. Exit 6 is its own outcome, not red and not a hollow finding (outline 9.4.2.3.4: a timed-out run is its own outcome, not red): it says the hollow did not finish, so there is no reading yet; today that outcome collapses into exit 0, which reads as a pass.
why: Measured 2026-11-21 on akiendelllinux: cdfc928cc5ff's hollow (323 commons records, ~17 s per tester run, ~93 min) was killed by prove.sh's `timeout 1500` at 25 min. prove.sh's last line pipes the hollow through `tail -4`, so prove.sh exited with tail's 0 and printed nothing under '--- hollow'; the walk went on to a confirmed verdict, and only the PROVED gate's hollow_evidence_absent caught it.
traces_to: Law 7 (errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces) and Law 8 (nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass): a ticket whose hollow outruns a fixed shell bound cannot be proved through prove.sh at all.
how: In cairn/devices/cc/scripts/prove.sh line 29, drop `timeout 1500`, keep `| tail -4` for display, read ${PIPESTATUS[0]}; on nonzero echo 'HOLLOW DID NOT FINISH (exit N)' and exit 6; name exit 6 in the header beside exit 5. Red-first proof runs the hollow step against a stub bin/cairn on PATH in a scratch house.

clauses.claim: with a stub hollow that exits nonzero (124, as a killed run does), prove.sh's hollow step exits 6 and prints a line containing 'HOLLOW DID NOT FINISH' and the exit status
with a stub hollow that exits 0, prove.sh's hollow step exits 0 and prints the hollow's last lines
prove.sh puts no wall-clock bound of its own on the hollow: a recording `timeout` first on PATH sees no invocation carrying --hollow

decisions.text: D1: prove.sh's hollow step drops the fixed timeout (the verb bounds each proof run at 120 s, cairn/devices/tester/hollow.py line 978, so a stuck run cannot hang it), takes the hollow's status from PIPESTATUS, and exits 6 with 'HOLLOW DID NOT FINISH (exit N)' on nonzero. The header names exit 6.
D2: the proof runs prove.sh's hollow step against a stub bin/cairn in a scratch house, one tooth per clause, stubbing the steps before it the way the sibling cc proofs do.

measured.saw: cdfc928cc5ff's prove run: '--- hollow' started 21:12 and printed nothing; prove.sh exited 0; verdict confirmed; close refused at 21:39 on hollow_evidence_absent
one tester run of cdfc's proof takes 17.3 s (the scan 0.09 s), so 324 hollow passes are about 93 min
measured.how: akiendelllinux_cc_0's timing, reported in its READY message for cdfc928cc5ff
